summary: Adversarially review the zero-config v3 diff for bugs that could affect the running local batch or users

findings.title: Once TURNS passes a stated budget, every later Stop check is cut down to missing_output only, and the text says 'turns left: -N'
findings.file_line: vacant_network/trace/zerostop.py:179 (last_turn = turns_left <= 1); vacant_network/adapters/agents.py:365 (TURNS never resets); vacant_network/trace/review.py:48 (turns_left_note)
findings.scenario: Scenario: interactive pi whose system prompt states a budget that is not enforced, for example via --append-system-prompt or AGENTS.md 'Use at most 20 steps'. The person runs one long request, or several requests in the same pi process. TURNS counts every turn in the process and never resets. `_budget_of` accepts turn > budget (it only checks budget > 0 and turn >= 0). After turn 19, every agent_before_settle stop call gets turns_left <= 1, which includes 0 and negative values. `_decide` sets last_turn=True and filters pushable down to missing_output. The other checks (unsourced value, failed step ignored, test claim, named file unread) are then never sent back for the rest of the process; they only go into the delivery note. When a missing_output line is sent, it says 'Model turns left in the stated budget: -12 of 20.' This silently turns off the default zero-config check. That check is the product's core (CLAUDE.md product principle 2), and the decision claims v3-3 applies 'only on the last turn'. Not triggered in the running DABstep batch: Harbor aborts at turn 15, so stop never runs with turns_left < 1.
findings.fix: Narrow only when turns_left == 1 exactly (or 0 < turns_left <= 1), and treat turns_left <= 0 as 'no budget information' (turns_left=None). In _budget_of, or in the JS stop payload, drop turn/budget when TURNS >= BUDGET. Add a test with turn > budget.

verdict.evidence:
Reproduced on both sides (the working tree's vacant_network matches 11f91f87).

JS side: I rendered PI_EXTENSION with ARGV pointed at a logging stub and drove it in node with a fake pi object (/tmp/claude-0/review_v3/turnsneg/js/drive.mjs and calls.log). The system prompt contained `<project_instructions path="/proj/AGENTS.md">Use at most 20 steps per task.`, so pi puts AGENTS.md into the system prompt through contextFiles (system-prompt.js:97). The first request ran 25 turns and the second request ran 3 more in the same session. The stop payloads were `{"turn":25,"budget":20}` and `{"turn":28,"budget":20}`. - The same state with turn=32/budget=20 returns `allow`, and both points go only into the note.
- turn=20/budget=20 (turns_left=0) gives the same result.
- With the answer file missing and turn=32/budget=20, the model receives "Model turns left in the stated budget: -12 of 20.", from review.py:48-50 via zerostop.py:179/193.

Nuance: the extension loader uses moduleCache:false and /new, /resume and /reload rebuild the runtime, so the scope is "until the session is replaced", not the whole process.

findings.title: Budget is taken from the first regex match anywhere in the system prompt, so project instructions win over the enforced cap
findings.scenario: Scenario: pi puts AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md into the system prompt (system-prompt.js project_context) before the text Harbor appends. Test on the shipped regex: 'Use at most 6 steps for a plan.\n\nYou have a hard budget of 15 model turns.' gives BUDGET=6, not 15. 'Plans should have up to 8 steps.' gives 8, and 'limit yourself to 10 iterations' gives 10. In any eval or CI repo with such a line, the reminder fires at turns 4-5, which the decision's own simulation found harmful. Stop narrowing starts at turn 5 and, combined with the finding above, stays on for the rest of the run, all on a cap nobody enforces. BUDGET is also latched on first read and never re-read. Not triggered in the running batch: the logged first requests contain no other match, and the first request is byte-identical across A/C1/C2 for tasks 9/44/51/62. It would bias any future run on repos with project instructions.
findings.fix: Prefer the last match (the harness text is appended at the end). Or match only the fixed 'hard budget of N ... turns' shape. Or skip the project_context/skills sections by reading ctx.getSystemPromptOptions() and applying the regex only to appendSystemPrompt/forceSystemPrompt deltas.

verdict.evidence:
Reproduced. Scratch files are in /tmp/claude-0/review_v3/budget_first/.

Code at 11f91f87 (vacant_network has not changed since then, up to HEAD): in vacant_network/adapters/agents.py, readBudget at lines 202-204 calls `BUDGET_RE.exec(text)`, which returns the first match only. BUDGET is set once at line 335 (before_agent_start) or line 367 (turn_end fallback) and never read again. BUDGET_RE_SRC is at line 405.

Why the first match is the wrong one: pi 0.87.1 `core/system-prompt.js` renders the sections in this order: preamble, tools, rules, docs, addendum, project_context (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md from cwd and its ancestors, via resource-loader.js loadProjectContextFiles), skills, cwd. Harbor's max-turns extension (pi.py:315-316) returns `systemPrompt: event.systemPrompt + "\n\nYou have a hard budget of N model turns..."`. The runner stores that as forceSystemPrompt (runner.js emitBeforeAgentStart), so the real budget text is the last thing in the prompt and every project instruction comes before it.

1) Regex alone (node, shipped JS regex), with a project_context line before the Harbor text:
- 'Use at most 6 steps for a plan.' gives 6
- 'Plans should have up to 8 steps.' gives 8
- 'limit yourself to 10 iterations' gives 10
- 'no more than 5 steps per migration' gives 5
- Harbor text alone gives 15

Worse variant: 'Use at most 2 steps per plan.' matches first with n<4, so readBudget returns null, the Harbor 15 is never considered, and v3 is silently off.

2) The generated extension itself (sim.mjs: template filled from agents_11f.py, fake pi/ctx, stub hook), 15 turn_end events with tool results:
- AGENTS.md 'Use at most 6 steps for a plan.': turn_check is sent after turns [4,5] with {"turn":4,"budget":6} and {"turn":5,"budget":6}.
- Neutral AGENTS.md: turns [13,14] with budget 15.
- 'Use at most 2 steps per plan.': never sent.

3) Real Python hook path (hook.handle("pi", ...) with the tests/test_zero_budget.py fixtures):
- turn_check turn=4 budget=6 gives action=continue: "Model turns left in the stated budget: 2 of 6. Write your current best answer ... now". The actual cap is 15.
- stop turn=9 budget=6 gives turns_left=-3. zerostop.py:179 `last_turn = turns_left <= 1` is true, so pushable is narrowed to missing_output only, and the text says "Model turns left in the stated budget: -3 of 6." TURNS is never reset, so this narrowing stays on for the rest of the process. The unsourced, failed-step, test-claim and unread checks are no longer sent back to the agent.

Without Harbor (normal interactive pi, no cap), the same AGENTS.md line creates a budget nobody enforces. That contradicts decision §四-1 ("only acts when the agent is told a turn cap").

Running experiment: not affected. I scanned all 363 v3local-tagged requests in the proxy log (scratchpad/local/ledger/io.jsonl). Every system prompt has exactly one regex match, 'budget of 15 model turns', so BUDGET=15 as intended.

Severity is minor. It needs specific wording in project instructions. When it triggers, it causes early reminders (which the decision's own simulation found harmful at early turns) and silently weakens the default Stop check for the rest of the session.

Fix: take the last match (Harbor appends at the end), or match only the fixed 'hard budget of N model turns' shape. A deltas-only approach would have to diff forceSystemPrompt, because Harbor passes the whole prompt through it.

findings.title: ended() note says 'after 16 of the stated 15 model turns' when the capped turn had tool calls
findings.file_line: vacant_network/adapters/agents.py:365 (TURNS += 1 on the post-abort turn_end); vacant_network/trace/zerostop.py:437-442
findings.scenario: Scenario: Harbor's max-turns extension calls ctx.abort() at turn_end #15. If assistant turn 15 contained tool calls, pi-agent-core's runLoop goes into one more iteration. streamAssistantResponse returns stopReason 'error' ('This operation was aborted') and no HTTP request is sent (ledger count stays 15). finishTurn then dispatches turn_end again, so TURNS=16. session_end sends turn=16, and ended() writes delivery.md with 'Ended before the agent said it was done, after 16 of the stated 15 model turns' and ended.turn=16. Confirmed on the live run v3local-g12-off-C2-44-s1: assistant #15 was [text, toolCall], #16 is error/aborted, and delivery.md and the chain 'ended' event both show 16. The human-facing note contradicts the cap. The ended.turn field is wrong for any analysis that reads it (the at_cap boolean and the note count are unaffected).
findings.fix: In the JS turn_end handler, do not increment TURNS, or do not report it, for a turn whose event.message.stopReason is 'aborted'/'error' with no tool calls when ctx.signal.aborted is already true. Or clamp in ended(): report min(turn, budget) and phrase it as 'at the stated cap of N model turns'.

verdict.evidence:
I reproduced this from the pi 0.87.1 source and from the live batch data.

Mechanism, from pi 0.87.1 sources:
- In pi-agent-core `dist/agent-loop.js` runLoop (L141-187), a turn whose message has tool calls sets `hasMoreToolCalls=true`.
- `config.finishTurn` then dispatches the extension `turn_end` boundary (`pi-coding-agent/dist/core/agent-session.js` L332-376).
- Harbor's max-turns extension (`harbor/agents/installed/pi.py` L319-323) calls `ctx.abort()` once `completedTurns>=15`. The loop still runs one more iteration.
- `streamAssistantResponse` then returns `stopReason 'error'` with "This operation was aborted". It emits `message_end`, so the message is persisted and the turn_end boundary can resolve its entry id. The error path (L143-152) calls `finishTurn` again, so extension turn_end runs a second time.
- The Vacant handler at `vacant_network/adapters/agents.py:365` (commit 11f91f87) does `TURNS += 1` on that call, making TURNS=16. `session_end` sends `turn: TURNS`.
- In `vacant_network/trace/zerostop.py:437-442`, `at_cap = 16>=15` is true, so the head line reads "after 16 of the stated 15 model turns".

Live data, run `scratchpad/local/formal_v3/g12-off-C2-s1/v3local-g12-off-C2-44-s1/dabstep-44__tqcLfcT/agent`:
- The pi session jsonl has 16 assistant messages. #15 is `stopReason toolUse` with content `[text, toolCall]`. #16 is `stopReason error`, "This operation was aborted", with empty content.
- `delivery.md` says "Ended before the agent said it was done, after 16 of the stated 15 model turns; no delivery check ran."
- `delivery.json` has `turn: 16, budget: 15`. The chain has an `ended` event.

Scope across the running batch so far: of 5 `ended_before_delivery` notes, 4 have (turn=16, budget=15) and 1 has (15, 15). So every capped run whose last turn called a tool gets the wrong count.

The nudge timing is not affected. TURNS matches Harbor's own `completedTurns` count at every pre-abort turn_end, and the extra increment happens only after the abort. The `at_cap` boolean stays correct.

Impact is limited to two things:
- The human-facing note contradicts the stated cap.
- The `turn` field in `delivery.json` and in the chain `ended` event is off by one for these runs.

Why this does not touch the running experiment:
- Nothing here is sent to the model.
- The reward comes from the verifier.
- `ops/eval/harbor_vacant.py` counts only `ended_notes`, not `turn`.
- `decisions/prereg/PREREG_20260926_ZERO_CONFIG_V3_LOCAL.md` does not reference the ended/turn fields.

findings.title: ended() writes a false 'Ended before the agent said it was done' note whenever the stop check did not append a review
findings.file_line: vacant_network/adapters/hook.py:393-395 (_zero_ended for every agent); vacant_network/trace/zerostop.py:~428-445 (ended: the only test is a 'review' event in the window)
findings.scenario: Scenario (a): `opencode run` in zero-config mode. The OpenCode plugin skips the stop check when NONINTERACTIVE (process.argv includes 'run'), then calls session_end on dispose with no reason. _zero_ended finds steps and no 'review' event, so every normally completed `opencode run` gets delivery.md saying 'Ended before the agent said it was done; no delivery check ran.' This is false: the agent finished, and Vacant chose not to check. Scenario (b): pi or Claude, where the stop check ran but returned without a review event (zerostop.stop timeout after CHECK_TIMEOUT_S, a child error, or out.ran False with 'why'). At quit, ended() writes the same false head. Case (b) can also overwrite the DID_NOT_RUN context. No effect on the model or on the running DABstep batch; it misleads the human reading the note.
findings.fix: Only write the 'ended before done' note when the session actually ended mid-work. For example, have the stop hook record a 'stop_seen' marker even when it allows without a review or times out, and check that marker in ended(). For OpenCode noninteractive runs, pass a flag and word the note as 'no delivery check ran (non-interactive run)'.

verdict.evidence:
I reproduced this at 11f91f87 (the vacant_network tree is identical to that commit). The script is /tmp/claude-0/review_v3/ended/repro.py and every event goes through the real hook.handle.

Why it happens: zerostop.ended() (vacant_network/trace/zerostop.py:409-465) decides that the agent never said it was done using only one test, whether a "review" or "ended" event exists in the window (line 428). zerostop.stop() appends a "review" event only inside _decide. It adds none in these cases:
- the child times out (the TimeoutExpired branch)
- the child raises an error
- _decide raises
- the check is deferred for subagents (hook.py:361-367)
- the stop check is skipped entirely
In all of these, hook.py:393-395 (_zero_ended) writes the "cut off" head at session_end.

(a) OpenCode `opencode run`. The plugin sets NONINTERACTIVE = process.argv.includes("run") (agents.py:499) and skips "stop" on idle (line 558). dispose then sends session_end with no reason (line 577). I replayed this through hook.handle("opencode", ...): a prompt, then a bash step that writes answer.txt, then session_end. The chain events were [trace_genesis, prompt, session_seen, step, ended, session_closed]. delivery.md said:
"- Ended before the agent said it was done; no delivery check ran.
- /app/answer.txt: exists; its content was not checked."
The agent finished normally; Vacant just chose not to check. Before v3 no note was written at session_end, so this is new in v3. It hits every zero-config `opencode run`, and it replaces any earlier delivery.md for that project.

(b) pi when _run_child raises TimeoutExpired. The stop call had final_text "The answer 2045 is in /app/answer.txt." and returned the DID_NOT_RUN note. After session_end reason=quit, delivery.md had the same false head "Ended before the agent said it was done". I got the same result when the child raises RuntimeError (case b2).

Control: with a normal stop check, a review event is appended and no ended note is written.

One sub-claim is weak. "Case (b) can overwrite the DID_NOT_RUN context" does not really hold. On timeout, DID_NOT_RUN appears only in the hook's return note and never in delivery.md. On a broken chain the chain is set aside, so ended() returns {} because chain_path is not a file. That does not change the main defect.

Effect: the model sees nothing, and scoring is unchanged. Only the note for the human is wrong. The same note also inflates harbor_vacant's descriptive "ended_notes" count, but only when the stop check errors or times out.

In the running batch (scratchpad local/formal_v3) I checked the 12 finished C2 vacant_check.json files:
- 7 have stop_reached=True, and all 7 have ended_notes=0.
- 5 have ended_notes=1, and all 5 are real cut-offs: reviews=0, 14-15 steps, nudges at turns 13/14.
- No false case has happened there so far.

findings.title: ended() skips the cut-off note whenever a 'continue' review exists, so the path v3-3 creates (last-turn pushback, then cut off by the cap) never gets a final note
findings.scenario: Harbor, max_turns=15. At turn 14 the agent says it is done without writing /app/answer.txt. stop is called with turns_left=1, so _decide appends review(action=continue), writes delivery.md with in_progress=True ('Turn ended ... (sent back for another pass)') and returns the missing-file pushback. At turn 15 the agent writes the file, and Harbor calls ctx.abort() in turn_end 15, so agent_before_settle never runs. session_end then calls ended(), and `any(e.type in ('review','ended'))` matches the continue review, so it returns early. I reproduced this with /tmp/claude-0/review_v3/test_scen.py::test_cutoff_after_last_turn_pushback_gets_no_final_note: ended count is 0, delivery.json has in_progress=true, and the note never says the run was cut off or whether answer.txt now exists. The same happens for any pushback at turn 13 or later followed by the cap. In the running batch, these C1/C2 runs are counted as stop_reached=true with ended_notes=0, so the prereg's descriptive counts of cut-off runs and ended notes are wrong. The primary endpoint is not affected.
findings.fix: Only skip when the latest review in this window has action=='allow', or an 'ended' event already exists. Continue reviews should not count. When the last review was a continue, write the ended note and list the files still missing from that round.

verdict.evidence:
The mechanism is real and I reproduced it, but the finding overstates both the severity and the effect on the running experiment.

Reproduced on the frozen code. vacant_network/ in the working tree is identical to 11f91f87. Command: /home/user/Vacant/.venv/bin/python -m pytest /tmp/claude-0/review_v3/test_scen.py::test_cutoff_after_last_turn_pushback_gets_no_final_note. The sequence goes through the real hook.handle("pi", ...): prompt, a bash step, then stop at turn 14 of budget 15. That returns action=continue (missing /app/answer.txt), and the review(action=continue) event is written. Then answer.txt is written and session_end(quit, turn=15) runs. Result: 0 'ended' events and delivery.json in_progress=true. delivery.md still reads "Turn ended: ... (sent back for another pass)". The md does not mention that answer.txt was missing when checked, that the run was cut off, or that the file exists now.

The pi 0.87.1 control flow confirms the real path. In dist/core/agent-session.js, _runAgentPrompt (around L1080) breaks out of the loop when _agentRunAbortRequested is set, before _runBeforeSettleBoundary. abort() (L1608) sets that flag, and ctx.abort() from an extension (L2450) calls it in print mode. Harbor's max-turns.ts (pi.py:319-323) calls ctx.abort() on turn_end 15. After that, dispose() emits session_shutdown reason "quit" (agent-session-runtime.js:297). So a pushback at turn 13 or 14 that is then cut off by the cap never reaches another stop. zerostop.ended() (11f91f87 zerostop.py:426-428) returns early because it sees the continue review. The same applies to any pushback followed by the cap or an Esc.

Why only minor, and why the running experiment is not affected:
(1) The skip matches what the code and decision say it should do. ended()'s docstring says "這個要求裡交件前檢查一次都沒跑", and DECISION v3-4 scopes the note to "交件前檢查沒跑到的那一跑". So this is a gap in what v3-4 covers, not code that departs from its spec.
(2) v3-3 does not create this path. In C1/v2 the Stop check already pushed back on the last turn, with every finding kind; v3-3 only narrows that to missing_output. The stale in_progress note after a pushback that is then cut off has existed since v2. v3 just doesn't cover it.
(3) The note goes only to the person. It is never sent to the model, so no model request and no reward changes.
(4) The prereg descriptive counts are not wrong. analyze_local.py sets stop_reached = runs with reviews. That is correct here, because the Stop check did run. ended_notes counts 'ended' events. The prereg defines that as notes for runs that "還沒說做完就結束", and in this scenario the agent did say it was done at turn 14. The prereg has no "cut-off runs" count; not-delivered runs are counted from answer_file/reward. C1 has no ended() at all, so C1's ended_notes is always 0 regardless.

What remains is a product flaw. After a last-turn pushback followed by the cap or an Esc, the person's final delivery note stays in the in-progress state. It says nothing about the cutoff or the requested file's final state. The finding's suggested fix is reasonable: skip only when the latest review in the window has action=allow or an ended event already exists.

findings.title: The stated budget is read from the whole system prompt, including the person's AGENTS.md, and TURNS never resets, so turns_left<=0 makes every later stop check return only missing_output and tells the model 'turns left: -N'
findings.scenario: Interactive pi (no real cap). The project AGENTS.md, which pi puts into the system prompt as <project_instructions>, says 'Keep any retry loop to at most 10 iterations.' readBudget sets BUDGET=10, because the first regex match wins even when a real cap sentence comes later. TURNS counts every model turn in the process and is never reset between requests. At process turns 8 and 9, any request that names an output file gets a nudge saying 'Model turns left in the stated budget: 2 of 10', which is false. From turn 9 on, every stop check gets turns_left<=0. `last_turn = turns_left <= 1` is then true for the rest of the session, so unsourced, failed_step, test_claim and unread pushbacks are silently removed (they only go into the note). The one pushback that still goes out says 'Model turns left in the stated budget: -25 of 5' (reproduced in test_scen.py::test_turns_left_negative_downgrades_stop). Under a real cap turns_left<=0 can never reach stop, so a value <=0 only happens when the budget was misread. The harm is to interactive users; DABstep /app has no AGENTS.md.
findings.fix: Treat the budget as unenforced when turns_left<=0: use `last_turn = turns_left == 1`, and ignore the budget and stop nudging once TURNS > BUDGET. Read the budget only from text outside <project_instructions>/skills, or take the last match (the harness appends its cap at the end) instead of the first. Also clamp turns_left_note so it never prints a value <=0.

verdict.evidence:
I reproduced this at commit 11f91f87 using sources exported with `git archive` to /tmp/claude-0/review_v3/f_budgetmisread/src, the real pi 0.87.1 system-prompt builder, and the real `hook.handle`.

(1) AGENTS.md is part of the text readBudget reads. pi 0.87.1 `core/agent-session.js:1003-1013` puts `getAgentsFiles()` into `_baseSystemPromptOptions.contextFiles`. `core/system-prompt.js` renders them as `<project_instructions>`, after the addendum. `emitBeforeAgentStart` (`runner.js:1016-1036`) exposes that rendered text as `event.systemPrompt`. readBudget (`agents.py:204`) runs `BUDGET_RE.exec` with no `g` flag, so the first match wins. It is read once and never re-read (`agents.py:335/367`).

(2) TURNS is a module-level counter (`agents.py:200`), and the only thing that ever changes it is `TURNS += 1` (`agents.py:365`). The extension loads once per session runtime (jiti, `moduleCache:false`), so TURNS keeps counting across every request in an interactive session.

Node harness: /tmp/claude-0/review_v3/f_budgetmisread/harness.mjs loads the generated extension, with ARGV pointed at a logging fake hook. The system prompt was built by pi's `buildSystemPrompt` with an AGENTS.md containing "Keep any retry loop to at most 10 iterations.", and there was no cap anywhere. I sent three requests with 7, 6 and 11 turns. The hook received:
- `stop {turn:7,budget:10}`
- `turn_check {turn:8,budget:10}` and `turn_check {turn:9,budget:10}`, both during request 2
- `stop {turn:13,budget:10}`
- `stop {turn:24,budget:10}`

Python, through the real `hook.handle('pi',...)` (/tmp/claude-0/review_v3/f_budgetmisread/src/tests/test_repro_misread.py):
(a) Same session state, stop without a budget: `continue`, with a pushback that data/sales.csv was never opened. With `turn=24, budget=10`: `{"action":"allow","reason":""}`. The pushback is silently dropped because `last_turn = turns_left <= 1` (`zerostop.py:179`) filters pushable down to `missing_output` only.
(b) `turn_check` at turns 8 and 9 with budget 10, for a request "write a summary ... to NOTES.md": the model is sent "Model turns left in the stated budget: 2 of 10" and then "1 of 10", although nothing enforces a cap.
(c) Stop with a missing NOTES.md at turn 24: the pushback reads "Model turns left in the stated budget: -14 of 10." (`review.turns_left_note`, `review.py:48`; `hook.py:306` passes `budget-turn` without clamping).

Because TURNS only grows, even a large misread number (for example "up to 100 iterations") eventually puts every later stop check of a long interactive session into last-turn mode. That silently weakens the default zero-config stop check, which is product principle 2. It also contradicts decision §四-1, which says v3 almost never fires in normal interactive use.

Why the running experiment is not affected: I ran BUDGET_RE_SRC over all of pi's `dist/core/**/*.js` and found no matches, so pi's default prompt text contains no match. The DABstep image (official Dockerfile plus the pinned FROM) puts only /app/data/* in /app and has no AGENTS.md. `vacant install` does not install the pi skill by default (skill=False). Harbor runs a single `pi --print` request per process, so TURNS starts at 0 and the only match is Harbor's appended "hard budget of 15 model turns" sentence.

findings.title: ended() treats 'no review event' as 'the agent never said it was done', so check errors, timeouts, deferral and `opencode run` all get a false 'Ended before the agent said it was done' note
findings.scenario: (a) The agent says it is done. zerostop.stop's child check times out (330 s) or raises, so it returns DID_NOT_RUN and no review event is written. At session_end the note says 'Ended before the agent said it was done; no delivery check ran.' and ended_notes goes up by 1 (reproduced in test_scen.py::test_stop_check_error_then_ended_note_claims_not_done). findings.title: ended() says its user_message is shown when there is a UI, but nothing ever shows it
findings.scenario: render() forwards user_message only for ev.kind == 'stop': Claude through systemMessage, and pi and OpenCode through `note`. For session_end, Claude and Codex render nothing. Pi's session_shutdown handler ignores the reply, and the OpenCode dispose() handler does too. The docstring says '`user_message` 只在有介面時會被顯示', and v3-4 is described as a note for the person. In practice the cut-off note is only a file under $VACANT_HOME/trace/projects/<proj>/delivery.md that nobody is pointed to, and the 'screen' lines built at zerostop.py:463 are never shown. The text claims more than the code does.
findings.fix: Either show it (for example, the pi extension calls ctx.ui.notify(d.note) on session_shutdown when hasUI, and render() passes `note` for session_end), or remove the claim and the dead screen lines and say plainly that the note is only written to the data folder.

verdict.evidence:
I reproduced this at commit 11f91f87. I extracted the files with `git archive` to /tmp/claude-0/review_v3/src_um, ran /tmp/claude-0/review_v3/um/repro.py, and sent a cut-off run through the real `hook.handle` for each agent: prompt, then `ls data` as pre and post, then session_end. In every case `zerostop.ended()` built a `user_message` and wrote delivery.md, and in every case `render()` dropped the message.
- pi (session_end, reason=quit, turn=15, budget=15) returned `{"action": "allow", "reason": ""}`.
- claude (SessionEnd) returned `('', '', 0)`, so there is no systemMessage.
- codex (SessionEnd) returned `('', '', 0)`.
- opencode (session_end) returned `{"action": "allow", "reason": ""}`.

For all four, the check "user_message shown in render output" came out False.

Why, in the code:
- `adapters/hook.py:143` sends systemMessage only when `ev.kind == "stop"`.
- `hook.py:154` adds `note` only when `ev.kind == "stop"`.
- At 11f91f87, the pi extension's `pi.on("session_shutdown")` (agents.py around lines 394-398) does `await ask(...)` and throws the reply away. The opencode `dispose()` (around lines 574-578) does the same. The only `ctx.ui.notify(d.note)` in the file is in `agent_before_settle`.
- The commit's own test (`tests/test_zero_budget.py`, test_a_run_cut_off_before_the_stop_check_still_gets_a_note_for_the_person) asserts `d == {"action": "allow", "reason": ""}` for session_end. So the `screen` lines built at zerostop.py:463-465 can never be shown. The docstring at zerostop.py:412 says "`user_message` 只在有介面時會被顯示" (shown only when there is a UI), which is not true.

In practice the only output is delivery.md under $VACANT_HOME/trace/projects/<hash>/, and nothing points the person to it.

The authors already agree. The v3.1 section of DECISION_20260926_ZERO_CONFIG_V3.md, in commit 5f3339df, says "說明只寫檔（工作階段結束時已經沒有畫面），文件改正" (the note is only written to a file; there is no screen at session end; docs corrected). That confirms the mismatch and that it was fixed later, not in the frozen wheel.

Why this is minor and does not touch the running experiment: the gap is between what the docstring promises and what the code does. Nothing is sent to the model either way. Harbor runs pi as `pi --print --mode json` (harbor pi.py:446), which has no UI, so the note would never be shown in C2 anyway. delivery.md is still written, and that file is what the analysis reads.

One housekeeping note: I first used `git worktree add` and then `remove`/`prune`, which touched /home/user/Vacant/.git/worktrees metadata. After that I switched to `git archive`, and no tracked files were modified.
